drift.anchor_note: the replay is indexed at this bar and the recorded nav is divided by this bar's nav: the shares are bought at the fill, so a mark before the fill would price them from a bar they did not exist on (r1585)
drift.identity_provisional_note: the ledger published these bars while the panel for their date was still gaining symbols; its own gate restates or promotes them, so this face prints their live deviation instead of failing on work that belongs to the producer
drift.identity_cause_note: PANEL_MOVED_SINCE = the closes this bar was marked on are no longer the closes on disk (baseline_stamped says the digest was taken after publication, so the move is dated from that stamp); PANEL_SAME = same closes, so a deviation there is the book's own; FP_BASELINE_ONLY = the digest was stamped after the fact and can only witness later revisions; NO_FP_LEGACY = published before the ledger recorded its closes

carry_coverage.note: bars beyond the repo ladder's last priced day are provisional: their cash leg is a forward-filled rate, so a NAV that disagrees with the re-derivation there measures the rate panel, not the book

drift.convention: ledger books constant target weights every bar (costless implicit rebalance) + carry on the target cash fraction; a card follower holds drifting weights, so nav_buyhold_gap is the convention's own footprint

caveats: Agreement is a snapshot of two records of one frozen decision; it does not make either record correct, and it will not catch a both-faces-wrong defect.
The card-config sheet is checked against the card because it is issued FROM it. It agreeing proves the derived face was republished, not that the card is right.
The drift cost is the price of restoring frozen weights today; the engine only pays it on a grid decision bar, so it is an upper bound on what drift costs.
A 3-bar ledger cannot resolve a return edge -- see the significance block in results/etf_book_forward/LEDGER.json. This face measures book-keeping, not skill.
